proposed_architecture_change: Introduce a physical-state substrate capability gate below Clay semantic authority. The authoritative SQLite WAL backing may enter release acceptance only when the exact runtime is upstream-fixed, carries independently verified downstream provenance for the exact fix, or an adversarially verified production topology makes the documented concurrent write/checkpoint precondition unreachable.
semantic_boundary: This is a physical persistence/recovery safety constraint. It does not create a second semantic architecture and does not move truth authority from Clay/UnifiedDB into SQLite.
strongest_counterhypothesis: Existing global execution serialization or Ubuntu downstream patching already removes the practical race without a runtime upgrade.
discriminating_tests: Target build-provenance receipt: dpkg version, _sqlite3 extension path, dynamic linked libsqlite3, CLI source/version and exact vendor patch evidence.
UnifiedDB topology discriminator: independently opened canonical-style connections, WAL mode, per-connection wal_autocheckpoint setting and production-equivalence review.
After any substrate mitigation, rerun WAL latency/contention/integrity, crash/recovery and UnifiedDB replay/effect atomicity tests.
rollback: All committed changes are additive diagnostics/workflow gates using disposable databases. Revert these commits if a superior accepted physical-state safety gate replaces them.
promotion_rule: Do not promote a clean race-canary result. Promotion requires positive patch provenance or positive topology exclusion plus matched target-VPS acceptance evidence.
